newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on Greenspan, certification.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on Greenspan, certification.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed sharply lower for the second day in a row on Thursday, dragged down by the U.S. market and fear of possible economic sanctions by Washington.
Dealers said month-end buying provided some relief in late trade, but a vicious circle triggered by external factors since Wednesday dragged share prices down for most of the day.

The leading IPC share index ended down 38.23 points, or 0.98 percent, at 3,851.92. On the broad market, 106 stocks changed hands, with decliners trouncing gainers by 63 to 20 on brisk volume of 92.6 million shares.

"The bourse was hit by a fall on Wall Street, lingering fallout from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony and concern over whether the U.S. government will certify us or not," said Esteban Rojas, deputy head of research at the Arka brokerage.
The U.S. government is expected to rate Mexico's cooperation in the war on drug-trafficking by the weekend. Failure to obtain certification could entail economic sanctions.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 58.11 points at 6,925.07, for a two-day loss of more than 100 points.
Greenspan hinted on Wednesday that the Fed may raise U.S. interest rates to contain inflationary pressures.

"All of this hampers the flow of foreign capital into Mexican financial markets and adds to the feeling that (domestic) interest rates have bottomed out, which can be seen from where the peso ended today," Rojas added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts weakened 17.6 centavos to close at 7.98 per dollar. It was the peso's sharpest daily decline since November 1995, when Mexico was in the throes of an economic crisis.
Telmex L shares, which accounted for more than 10 percent of all shares traded, ended up 8 centavos (1 cent) at 15.50 pesos ($1.94), while its ADRs fell 1/4 to 38-7/8 on Wall Street.

Food company Grupo Corvi led the decliners in the wake of what analysts said were poor earnings, posted after the close of trade on Wednesday. Corvi ended off 54 centavos (7 cents) at 5.60 pesos (70 cents).
Other notable decliners were financial group GFNorte, off 46 centavos (6 cents) at 8.78 pesos ($1.10), and media group Televisa, which plunged 5.00 pesos (63 cents) to 96.00 pesos ($12.03).
